title: Rabbi Chiyya of Tzippori
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Ami’s student, as in Jerusalem Talmud Orlah, chapter 3, beginning of halakhah 2, where he raised an objection before Rabbi Imi. He was a Kohen, as at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, chapter 11: Rabbi Chananyah bar Akbari used to work with Rabbi Chiyya of Tzippori; when he left him, he would fill a lamp for him with impure terumah oil for burning, etc. In Midrash Tehillim 12:1: “Rabbi Chiyya of Tzippori went to buy wheat in Sura; Yonatan said to him: When you want to buy wheat, say ‘I want barley,’” etc. Seder HaDorot writes to see the entry Rav Huna of Tzippori, thinking they are one; Hyman distinguishes them: the first was Rabbi Ami’s student, and Rav Huna of Tzippori was Rabbi Yochanan’s student.

notes.text: The Terumot chapter/halakhah reference is Jerusalem Talmud; שמן שריפה is impure terumah oil designated for burning. Hyman’s distinction from Rav Huna of Tzippori is retained rather than merged.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 11 directly names Chananyah bar Akbari working with Rabbi Chiyya Tzipporaya and the burning-oil lamp. The full context distinguishes permitted priestly needs from an Israelite’s needs. Hyman’s priesthood inference, other transmissions and distinction from Huna of Tzippori remain attributed.
